messages:
pagerduty: P1 ALERT — runtime-serving-prod: repeated model load/warmup failures for model-x-large in us-west-1. Symptoms: CUDA OOM during model deserialization and occasional container crash / node flapping. Runbook link: /incidents/runbooks/model-load.md

infra-bot: detected 14 failed warmup attempts across 6 pods in ds-runtime-pool-3 within 5m. Recent errors: OOM, DeserializationError, nvrtc compile timeout.

alice (oncall-sre): ack — paging runtime eng. I'm jumping in and will triage the cluster.

bob (runtime-eng): on it. can you post pod names? I'll start with logs.

alice (oncall-sre): pods: ds-runtime-pool-3-5b9c, ds-runtime-pool-3-9f2d, ds-runtime-pool-3-b7a1. curl health shows 503 on ds-runtime-pool-3-5b9c.

charlie (ml-runtime): quick context: model-x-large has a heavy warmup (large KV cache). We recently pushed a JIT compile tweak in v2.1.0 that increased memory footprint during load.

bob (runtime-eng): pulling logs now. snippet from ds-runtime-pool-3-5b9c:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 14.10 GiB already allocated)
  at /pytorch/aten/src/..: allocate.cpp:xx
DeserializationError: unexpected EOF while reading storage for tensor 'transformer.wte.weight'
```

alice (oncall-sre): looks like OOM at deserialization step, not during inference. pods crash during model.load(). Some nodes log nvrtc: compile timeout for fused-kernel.

dana (platform): checking node status — 2 nodes in the pool reported kubelet restarted in last 10m. Could be memory pressure from concurrent warmups. Autoscaler did not add nodes because reserved capacity hit.

erin (support): any customer impact? I'm seeing 3 enterprise tenants with elevated 500s in us-west-1 for generation endpoints pointing to model-x-large.

james (customer-success): pinged those customers via email + incident Slack thread; letting them know engineering is investigating.

bob (runtime-eng): immediate mitigation options: 1) disable warmup for model-x-large cluster-wide (fast, low-risk) 2) fallback traffic to model-x-large-quant8 (smaller memory) 3) rollback recent JIT compile flag change in the runtime (requires deploy). Which order?

alice (oncall-sre): do 1 and 2 in parallel. disable warmup on affected pool and route traffic to quant8 variant. if request latencies acceptable, escalate to platform to add nodes.

charlie (ml-runtime): note: quant8 variant has slightly lower quality on some prompts. we should gate it to only affected customers or to a global fallback with banner.

alice (oncall-sre): executing: kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n svc --patch "{\"data\":{\"warmup_enabled\":\"false\"}}" for ds-runtime-pool-3

infra-bot: config applied to ds-runtime-pool-3. Warmup disabled.

bob (runtime-eng): reroute command: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/routes/switch -d '{"cluster":"ds-runtime-pool-3","to_model":"model-x-large-quant8"}' — result: 202 accepted.

alice (oncall-sre): restarting crashed pods after config change: kubectl rollout restart ds/ds-runtime-pool-3 -n svc

infra-bot: rollout started. pods rebooting.

bob (runtime-eng): watching logs — new pods load quant8 model successfully. no OOM in first 3 minutes.

erin (support): observed customer 500s drop from 18% -> 2% for tenant-omega within 4 minutes. reporting as degraded but serving.

charlie (ml-runtime): to prevent recurrence we should: 1) revert the JIT memory-heavy compile flag 2) add warmup concurrency limit 3) add a pre-check to fall back to quantized model if deserialization would exceed X GiB. I'll draft PRs.

dana (platform): I'll temporarily increase reserved nodes for ds-runtime-pool-3 by +2 nodes to give room for background loads while we assess. Doing cloud request now.

alice (oncall-sre): status update: impact reduced — all affected pods now running quant8 fallback, errors reduced, some requests see quality regression. Marking incident as mitigated->degraded.

pagerduty: incident severity remains P1 until root cause confirmed and rollback plan scheduled.

bob (runtime-eng): reproduction notes — on a staging GPU with same model and a cold start we can reproduce OOM by forcing full pre-warm using
```
python -c "from runtime import load_model; load_model('model-x-large', warmup=True)"
```
OOM triggers at the deserialization step for weight blocks > 1GB. nvrtc compile timeouts observed when more than 6 warmups run concurrently.

charlie (ml-runtime): temporary config change we'll propose in a PR: warmup.max_concurrency=2; warmup.memory_guard=12GiB; fallback.threshold=0.85 (based on token distribution).

erin (support): impacted customers list: tenant-omega, tenant-zenith, tenant-acme-corp. I've opened high-priority support cases and included mitigation notes.

james (customer-success): customers acknowledged fallback and prefer fail-open (degraded quality) over 500s. Two customers requested opt-out for fallback — we've noted for later.

alice (oncall-sre): handoff: I'm going off shift in 25m. bob, can you take incident lead for next 8h? Ensure rollback PR and metrics dashboard.

bob (runtime-eng): taking over. I'll open a tracking ticket and schedule a hotfix deploy to revert the JIT flag and add warmup concurrency guard.

dana (platform): cloud request approved. +2 nodes added to pool. Observability: memory pressure metrics now within normal after fallback.

alice (oncall-sre): quick checklist before I sign off: 1) Disable warmup — done 2) Fallback -> quant8 — done 3) Restart pods — done 4) Added nodes — pending -> now done 5) Customer comms — erin/james — done

alice (oncall-sre): tagging incident P1 -> mitigated (degraded) and leaving notes for postmortem. I'll create the initial timeline in the incident doc.

bob (runtime-eng): created ticket RUNTIME-2319: revert JIT flag + warmup limits + telemetry for deserialization memory. Assigning charlie/dana.

charlie (ml-runtime): I'll start PR for fallback pre-checks and memory guards. Also adding a deserialization stream mode to avoid full materialization of huge tensors during load.

pagerduty: note: escalation policy notified execs.

erin (support): closing customer cases as 'service degraded' until we finalize fix; customers ok for now.

bob (runtime-eng): next steps: hotfix rollback staged for canary on us-west-1 tomorrow 03:00 UTC, monitor for 2h, then roll to prod if green. Postmortem owner: alice + bob + charlie.

alice (oncall-sre): thanks everyone — handing off. I'll be reachable on pager if things regress. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident state changed: mitigated -> monitoring.

bob (runtime-eng): final note: include commit id of last runtime change in postmortem; looks like 7f3a2b1 bumped JIT optimizations. We'll correlate memory changes to that commit.

charlie (ml-runtime): logging todo: add heap snapshots on model load failure, and better error mapping for DeserializationError.

alice (oncall-sre): end of thread for now. Postmortem link will be shared once created.
